findings.title: Untrusted source attribute is not escaped
findings.why: `source` is interpolated into the opening `<untrusted source="...">` tag without escaping. Repository paths used as sources (nested AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md paths and module paths) can contain quotes and `</untrusted>`, which can close the data block or forge tags, letting attacker-controlled names escape the data context.

findings.title: Module path is outside the untrusted block in the summary prompt
findings.why: `Module: {path}` is placed before the `<untrusted>` block. Directory names are repository content, so a crafted directory name can inject instructions that are not marked as data and can steer the finder model's summary.

findings.title: Layer cache key ignores skip_paths
findings.why: The cached conventions and directory tree depend on `skip_paths`, but `_key` hashes only tree id, LAYER_VERSION and memory_version. Changing skip rules reuses stale conventions/tree (showing skipped files or omitting newly included ones) while module summaries use the new rules.

findings.title: summary budget setting is never wired
findings.why: `summary_tokens_per_build` is added as the cost safety net, but no code in this change reads it to construct a TokenBudget/UsageMeter. `module_summaries` only stops on a BudgetExceededError supplied by an external `summarize`, so the default summary path has no enforced cap.

findings.title: Sample truncation can exceed the token budget for wide characters
findings.why: The excerpt length assumes four characters per token, but `estimate_tokens` counts non-ASCII characters as roughly one token each. A CJK-heavy file can produce an excerpt up to four times the remaining `_SAMPLE_TOKENS`, blowing the sample/context budget.

findings.title: read_text scans the full file list for every lookup
findings.why: `read_text` linearly searches `self.files()` on each call. `sample_module` calls it per module file, making summary generation O(files^2) on large repositories and potentially very slow.

findings.title: Recursive module splitting can hit Python recursion limit
findings.why: `subtree` and `marked_below` recurse once per directory level. A repository with a deep enough tree (within git path limits) raises RecursionError and aborts context construction.
